questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A mix of different things. I wanted an english speaking country to improve my english skills and to explore the Irish culture and meet the Irish people which I heard a lot of good stories about before going.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My overall experience is actually a 11 out 10. Accepting the exchange spot in Limerick was truly the best decision made. First of all is the Irish culture absolutely amazing. People are so kind, open and welcoming, which gave me the feeling of being part of the culture very quickly. I made a lot of new friends - both other internationals and Irish - which was the best way to exchange cultural experiences. The University of Limerick (UL) offers a lot of interesting courses, the professors are competent and UL is very progressive and including in many ways. Campus holds a lot of different faculties so you get the chance to meet people who study different educations than yourself and you can join a lot of very nice sports and social clubs and societies on campus. A lot of young people live in Limerick and the Castletroy area, which gives you the feeling of living in a 'study city'. Ireland has A LOT of pubs, Guinness and truly amazing nature that calls for a lot of hikes. I really recommend everyone to go on exchange in Limerick. I was so happy that I did and I wished that I could attend an extra semester myself!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
It was very easy! University of Limerick provided me with all information needed. Students had the chance to attend two weeks online orientation before semester start. My academic coordinator at UL was very helpful and replied to emails very quickly, which was very helpful. 

The reason that I dont rate the assistance 5 out of 5 is due to accommodation issues. Unfortunately, I did not get a spot on the on-campus accommodation. Therefore I had to find accommodation on my own, which was very difficult (due to housing crisis in Ireland) and the assistance from the university was very little.. They tried to provide students without accommodations with websites etc. but it was still very difficult and I felt a bit 'left alone'.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: All internationals got picked up in the airport in Dublin.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: UL staff are very friendly and helpful regarding all academic inquries!

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Unfortunately, it was very difficult. The university do not have enough on-campus rooms available to all internationals. At the moment the housing situation in Limerick - and Ireland in general - is very bad. It was more difficult to find accommodation than I expected. I ended up in an Airbnb with 3 other international students in Limerick city 5 KM from campus and it was very overpriced. I hope that the housing situation will get better very soon. 

BUT! even though I had some difficulties finding accommodation did it not affect my overall experience and it was a very good experience to live in a small apartment with three other internationals. I mean how often do you get that chance? We had a very good and fun time that I appreciate a lot.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I lived in the city and travelled to university by bus. I bought a monthly travel card for €52. The busses are not as good as in Copenhagen and they do not drive in the night time. Get some on-campus friends and sleep at their place after parties or use Free-now taxi service. 

Some of my other friends living off-campus travelled by bike - but Irish people do not bike as much as Danish people and bike lanes are a bit rare in Limerick.  

I REALLY recommend looking for accommodation in Castletroy in a walking distance to UL. Areas such as Milford, Oaklawns, Elm Park and College Court are VERY nice and lots of irish students live together in big houses. If I were staying for two semesters I would move to one of these areas.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Don't give up. Housing can be difficult but it is worth the effort.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Don't stress about the courses registration. You have a three weeks to figure out which courses you wanna attend before signing up for good. You can always change your learning agreement if you choose to take another course than the one you planned to take before going to Ireland.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
In the first two weeks internationals students have the chance to attend different courses before registration. I found all my courses before going to Limerick but it was great that we got the opportunity to try out different courses in the beginning. 

International students create their own timetable, which might seem a bit difficult because you are responsible for not choosing courses that are overlapping. I was very lucky that all the courses that I wanted to attend were available and did not overlap.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The academic coordinators at UL were very helpful. In the orientation weeks they provided us with the information needed about course registration and they sent a lot of documents and guidelines on email as well.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up getting all the classes I registered for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you have any difficulties then ask your academic coordinator or the professors in the courses that you attend. They are all very helpful. Things will work out as soon as you get to UL so do not stress it!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UL offers a range of very interesting courses and the professors are very competent. Being part of an english speaking academic environment is a very good way to improve your academic english very quickly.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level at UL is a bit lower than UCPH but for me that was not a problem. The lectures and readings were very interesting.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I attended two lectures and one tutorial each week. In the tutorials the weekly assignments were discussed, which was very helpful and interesting and a good way to participate in class-discussions with other students.  

The workload at UL compared to UCPH was a bit bigger each week. Students were to hand-in small assignments before attending lectures and tutorials. We also did a presentation in one of my courses. Both weekly assignments and presentations are a part of the final grade. The reading workload every week was smaller than at UCPH (and all the reading are free!!). 

I handed in a larger assignment in all of my 5 courses at mid-term and in the end of the term. I had no oral or sit-in exams. You have to hand-in all your assignments on your own. In my courses groups were not a choice, unfortunately.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
I attended 5 different courses: 
Nationalism, Ethnicity and Conflict
Policy-Making in the European Union
Comparative European Politics
Sociology of Gender and Popular Culture 
International Organizations and Global Governance

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I REALLY enjoyed Nationalism, Ethnicity and Conflict, Sociology of Gender and Popular Culture and Policy-Making in the European Union. But the professors in all courses were very engaged, competent and helpful. My two other courses were a bit of a repetition of courses that I already attended at UCPH.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Housing was more expensive than expected. 
I chose to spend a lot of money going on weekend trips with my friends. That was really worth it!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is cheaper than in DK if you go to Aldi or Lidl. Spar, Tesco and Dunnes Store are a bit more expensive but still cheaper than DK. Lunch at UL are the same prices as at UCPH.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My biggest recommendation is to join a club! I had SO much fun in the clubs that I joined and I got so many new friends.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
UL offers so many different sports clubs and societies. I was so surprised but it is an amazing way to make new friends - especially local friends - with same interests as you! I joined the UL kayak club, which was so much fun and a VERY good way to get to know lots of Irish students. We went on a weekend-trip, a lot of river trips and pool sessions every week. I also joined the Outdoor Pursuit club, which offered climbing and hike-trips. Unfortunately, it was very difficult to get a spot on the hike-trips due to the big demand so I ended up going on hikes with my friends on our own. But the climbing sessions were very good. 

Other than that UL arrange day-trips around Ireland throughout the semester. I joined a trip in the beginning and that was a very good experience and a cheap way to get to see new places in Ireland.

The university pub 'Stables' has an international night every friday which is a very nice way to end the week!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
If you wanna experience the real Irish craic then join the kayak club ;-). 

All international students are very friendly and open! Join the social events in the beginning of the semester to meet all the other Erasmus students. We had some big Whats-app groups where international students organized social meet ups and parties throughout the semester. That was very nice.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I really recommend going on weekend trips. I arranged a trip with my other international friends almost every weekend. We used GoCar which is a cheap and easy solution. It is way easier to go by car and you get used to the traffic very quickly! Hostels are OK cheap as well. 

We did a lot of amazing hikes in Killarney National Park, Wicklow Mountains, Sligo, Dingle Penninsula, Waterford and Connemara National Park. The nature is SO stunning so bring some good hiking boots, download the hiking app "Alltrails" and go explore! You won't get disappointed. 

We also visited the big cities; Dublin, Cork, Galway and Belfast in Northern Ireland. These places are 'must see' as well! 

Most Irish people travel home to their parents in the weekends so most going outs, house parties and social events with irish people are during the week. 

If you are going to Limerick during the fall semester then remember to attend 'Christmas Day' in November - ask an Irish friend for more information. Promise me! you don't wanna miss out on that one!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - Irish people are the best people! For me Limerick felt like home very quickly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Again; JOIN A CLUB! All my Irish friends are people that I met in my clubs - especially the kayak club. We did a lot of parties together and a Christmas Dinner in December. For me that was the absolutely best way to get to know Irish people and the Irish culture.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The accent is lovely but can be difficult at times ;-)  and then the Irish slang. Get some Irish friends who can teach you about 'craic', 'sound', 'class' and all the other words that they use all the time ;-).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Irish people are so friendly. I really appreciate that I got so many nice Irish friends while staying in Limerick.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Really enjoy your time in Limerick! Time is running way too fast. 

- Join as much social events as possible! Go on trips around Ireland, join clubs and go to house parties. (Yes, the house parties in College Court are as good as they say - don't miss out ;) )

- Don't stress too much about the academics. The Professors are so helpful and they check-up on the students throughout the semester, you will get used to writing in english very quickly and assignments and exams are doable.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Spend some time on finding accommodation if you don't get on-campus accommodation. Start as early as possible!!. It can be difficult but don't give up! Try to call a lot of landlords instead of emailing and do skype-calls before paying anything! Join the 'UL freshers' groups or 'rent in Limerick' on Facebook. In these groups other students are looking for roomies and landlords are looking for tenants. Airbnb is a solution as well, but unfortunately landlords charge very high rents at the moment.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I am very thankful that I got to know the Irish culture and that I got so many good new friends - both Irish and other internationals. Limerick might seem as a very small city, but trust me! It has so much to offer. I REALLY enjoyed my stay and I will recommend everyone to go on exchange at UL. My exchange in Ireland was beating all my expectations. It was four very very happy months!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The only challenge was that the semester ended and I had to leave Ireland.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just do it! Limerick is the best second-home you could ever wish for.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
